meta.headline: **Partial implementation (B)** is the dominant outcome (142 of 267 recommendations), and Hungary gives a National Report that admits "very limited progress": Act X of 2023 strengthened the National Judicial Council, a preventive restraining order that outlasts imprisonment (2025) and a review of 31,139 police domestic-violence cases, hate-crime training for all police, the National Strategy against Antisemitism (2024), the 2025 action plan under the Social Inclusion Strategy 2030, a partial decriminalisation of defamation (2023) and an Act on anti-discrimination in education (2024). **No relevant action (C)** covers 93 recommendations, notably media pluralism, civil-society space, asylum and pushbacks, the Istanbul Convention and the Women, Peace and Security plan. **Contrary measures (E)** apply to 16 recommendations: the 'child protection' law kept and extended by Act III of 2025, which bans Pride and other LGBTIQ-themed assemblies (a constitutional amendment followed), and the withdrawal from the Rome Statute. Four recommendations reach **A** (support for the family, visible bilingualism in the Rába region, cooperation with special procedures).

evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/1), para. 110 — Hungary: "Complex Settlement Programmes, reaching 80 segregated localities, contribute to reducing territorial inequalities and residential segregation"
UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/2), para. 68 — Special Rapporteur on freedom of religion: "51 per cent of Roma children dropping out while still in compulsory school"

recommendations.text: Combat intolerance and discrimination against members of vulnerable groups, including refugees, asylum seekers, migrants, women and girls, Roma, Muslims, Jews and LGBTQI+ persons. This effort should include discouraging intolerant rhetoric and repealing laws that ban public depictions of LGBTQI+ persons in the media and that refuse to legally recognize trans individuals’ gender identity

Improve the systems for the prevention, reporting, investigation and prosecution of hate crimes, incitement to violence and discrimination against migrants, refugees, Roma and lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender people
Strengthen measures to combat hate speech and hate crime, especially when targeted towards lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and intersex persons, asylum seekers, migrants and Roma
Activate efforts to prevent and eliminate all manifestations of intolerance on national basis, also decisively condemn any hate speech, including against Roma
Strengthen efforts to promote non-discriminatory access of members of the Roma community to existing social services
Take measures to combat discrimination and the spreading of hate speech against migrants and refugees, especially Roma

Strengthen measures to prevent racial hate crimes, the incitement of violence, and related discriminatory behaviour against refugees, migrants, Roma and other ethnic and sexual minorities, including by State officials, and ensure the effective registration, investigation and prosecution of all reported hate crimes
Take further steps to eliminate discrimination against the Roma population, especially in the fields of education, health and employment
Step up efforts to address discrimination and social exclusion faced by Roma with particular emphasis on integrated schooling
Further ensure that the Roma can access social services, including health care, education and employment, without discrimination
Continue to step up actions to increase the employment rate and conditions for women, with a focus on Roma women
Strengthen measures to eliminate discrimination against Roma children
Continue efforts to better integrate the Roma community into society
Continue to combat discrimination against the Roma community, particularly women and children, and promote their full social integration into the community
Redouble efforts to combat all forms of discrimination against groups in vulnerable situations, such as Roma, refugees and migrants, within the framework of Sustainable Development Goal 10
Strengthen laws to eradicate stereotyping and discrimination against migrants, refugees, Jews and Roma

blocks.summary: Repeal or revise the 'child protection'/anti-LGBTQI legislation and the adoption restrictions
blocks.meaning: Information or measures taken are contrary to, or reflect rejection of, the recommendation
blocks.rationale: Hungary kept the 2021 'child protection' law, which the CJEU found to breach Article 2 TEU, and in March 2025 extended it through Act III of 2025, which bans LGBTIQ-themed assemblies, followed by a constitutional amendment: measures contrary to the recommendation. Special procedures and OHCHR urged repeal.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/1), para. 101 — Hungary: "the Court of Justice of the European Union found, among other things, a violation of Article 2 of the TEU due to the homophobic nature of the so-called “child protection” law"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/2), para. 71 — Several special procedure mandate holders: "reiterated strong concerns about the legislative amendments introduced in March 2025, which effectively banned LGBTIQ-themed assemblies in Hungary"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/3), para. 64 — JS5: "immediately repeal the amendments introduced by Act LXXIX of 2021"

recommendations.text: Promote and fully respect the rights of lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and intersex people and the removal of stigmatizing and discriminatory provisions against them

Review anti-paedophilia legislation in accordance with its international human rights obligations to ensure that it focuses on combating this serious problem, including by removing provisions contrary to the human rights of the lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and intersex population

Prevent discrimination against lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and intersex persons by repealing laws that prohibit certain discussions about sexual orientation and gender identity with those under the age of 18 years
Abolish discriminatory legislative provisions vis-à-vis LGBTQI persons

Take all the necessary steps to end stigmatization of and discrimination against the LGBTI+ community, including by repealing legislation that uses child protection as a pretext for further marginalizing LGBTI+ persons

Take effective measures to prevent and prohibit discrimination against lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and intersex people, including by revoking the anti-lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and intersex provisions of the anti-paedophilia law and re-establishing the Equal Treatment Authority
Repeal the legislation banning the “promotion of homosexuality” among minors, and enact legislation to protect lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and intersex persons from discriminatory practices

recommendations.by: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
recommendations.text: Repeal discriminatory legislation, including the 2020 amendments restricting adoptions for same-sex couples
Revoke discriminatory provisions in the anti-paedophilia law, and actively promote tolerance and respect for persons with diverse sexual orientations and gender identities
Repeal the articles of the "Anti-Paedophilia Law" that prohibit the representation of gender identity other than the sex of birth, the change of sex and homosexuality

Adopt a comprehensive strategy and plan of action, including repealing any restrictive or discriminatory legislation, to ensure and uphold the equality and dignity of all human beings irrespective of their sexual orientation or gender identity

Revoke the new legislation purporting to protect children, which stigmatizes and discriminates against persons based on their sexual orientation and gender identity and establishes inadmissible links between homosexuality and paedophilia

blocks.summary: Protect LGBTQI persons: anti-discrimination law, gender recognition, strategy and education
blocks.rationale: The National Report cites only the pre-existing Equal Treatment Act, which already lists sexual orientation, and a police network of specialised investigators; no strategy, legal gender recognition or anti-discrimination reform is reported, and CEDAW notes unrecognised same-sex partnerships.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/1), para. 101 — Hungary: "Section 8 of Act CXXV of 2003 on Equal Treatment and the Promotion of Equal Opportunities explicitly mentions sexual orientation as prohibited grounds of discrimination"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/2), para. 74 — Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination against Women: "registered partnerships were not recognized under the joint and second parent adoption scheme"

recommendations.text: Take steps to protect the rights of lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and intersex persons, in particular allowing authorities to change the designation of the gender of individuals in official documents to reflect their gender identity
Implement additional measures aimed at the promotion of equal rights considering the law on lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and intersex persons

Take concrete measures to prevent and prohibit discrimination against LGBTQI people, and specifically same-sex couples and their children, in the fields of employment, education, health care and access to social benefits

Develop a national action plan to combat discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity and promote awareness-raising campaigns to combat stigmatization and bullying against lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and intersex persons
Make progress in the development of anti-discrimination legislation so that it specifically includes discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity
Revert the current ban on legal gender recognition and develop a procedure for recognition based on personal autonomy and self-identification
Guarantee the right of children to comprehensive sexuality education, including on the full diversity of sexual orientations, gender identities and sex characteristics

blocks.summary: Prevent discrimination and xenophobia against migrants, refugees and asylum seekers
blocks.rationale: The National Report contains no measure; UNHCR urges Hungary to address xenophobia against refugees, and the Special Rapporteur on freedom of religion reports anti-migrant rhetoric from high-level officials.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/2), para. 12 — UNHCR: "urged Hungary to address discrimination and xenophobia, in particular against refugees and asylum-seekers"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/2), para. 78 — Special Rapporteur on freedom of religion: "requested that Hungary confront the discriminatory anti-migrant and racist rhetoric that had marred the political and media space, had put asylum-seekers at risk of refoulement"

recommendations.text: Take concrete measures to ensure that migrants, refugees and asylum seekers can enjoy the rights to education, to health and to legal aid without discrimination
Intensify efforts to eliminate stereotypes and discrimination against migrants, refugees and national minorities
Continue to take specific measures to prevent and eliminate racism, racial discrimination, xenophobia and intolerance against migrants, refugees and asylum seekers
Strengthen and implement relevant legislation to eliminate discrimination against migrant workers, refugees and asylum seekers
Adopt measures to ensure that asylum seekers and refugees do not suffer discrimination and xenophobia

blocks.summary: Promote the use of minority languages in public life
blocks.rationale: Official documents and declarations have been available in Slovak, Serbian, Slovenian, Croatian, German and Romanian since 2022-2023, and Rába-region offices employ Slovenian speakers.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/1), para. 106 — Hungary: "In the Rába Region all municipal offices have Slovenian-speaking staff"

recommendations.text: Promote the use of minority languages in the public sphere and encourage their use in relations with administrative authorities
Promote of the use of the Slovenian language in public life

blocks.summary: Finance and broadcast minority-language media
blocks.rationale: The documents contain no information on this recommendation.

recommendations.text: Ensure proper financing of media in minority languages and extend the duration of television programmes in order to properly promote the minority languages
Increase the scope and frequency of radio and television programmes in the Slovenian language

blocks.summary: Restore media independence and the independence of the Media Council
blocks.rationale: The National Report has no media section; the Special Rapporteur on freedom of expression still calls for a reformed Media Council and a framework for media independence.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/2), para. 28 — Special Rapporteur on freedom of expression: "revise the appointment procedure for the Chair of the Media Council to make it more transparent and inclusive"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/2), para. 29 — Special Rapporteur on freedom of expression: "called for the independence, transparency and accountability of the Media Council, including through legislative reforms"

recommendations.text: Increase media independence by eliminating political bias in the National Media Council, allocating State advertising funds equitably to all outlets, and restoring the independence of the public broadcaster

blocks.summary: Support Council of the EU conclusions on the children's rights strategy
blocks.rationale: The documents contain no information on this recommendation.

recommendations.text: Support the adoption of the Council of the European Union conclusions on the new European Union strategy on children’s rights, and ensure, at national level, that all textbooks and other teaching materials address sexual orientation and gender identity in an objective way and promote tolerance and respect for LGBTI+ people

blocks.summary: Re-establish the Equal Treatment Authority
blocks.rationale: The National Report states that equal-treatment procedures are handled by the Commissioner for Fundamental Rights; the Authority was not re-established.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/1), para. 16 — Hungary: "The activities of the Commissioner for Fundamental Rights include responsibilities related to equal treatment, within which administrative authority procedures may be conducted and sanctions imposed"

recommendations.text: Re-establish the Equal Treatment Authority, and adopt a comprehensive strategy and action plan to tackle discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity

blocks.summary: Increase women's representation in senior positions
blocks.rationale: A bill on gender balance among directors of listed companies (EU Directive 2022/2381) was submitted to the National Assembly on 29 October 2024; no measure on political representation is reported.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/1), para. 35 — Hungary: "a draft law was submitted to the National Assembly on 29 October 2024"

recommendations.text: Increase women’s representation in political life and in senior positions in the public administration, as well as to prevent and combat women’s stereotyping and discrimination, including sexist rhetoric

blocks.summary: Guarantee the right of asylum
blocks.rationale: The National Report is silent on asylum; stakeholders report continuing pushbacks.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/3), para. 68 — JS4: "ending the practice of pushbacks at Hungary’s borders"

recommendations.text: Take concrete measures to ensure effective exercise of the right of asylum and adopt a strategy to combat violence linked to racial discrimination, hate crimes and hate speech

blocks.summary: Protect freedom of association, peaceful assembly and expression
blocks.meaning: Information or measures taken are contrary to, or reflect rejection of, the recommendation
blocks.rationale: In 2025 Parliament adopted Act III of 2025 amending the Right of Assembly Act, which effectively bans Pride and other assemblies deemed to violate the 'child protection' laws, with fines for participants and criminal liability for organisers, later reinforced by a constitutional amendment: a measure contrary to the recommendation.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/3), para. 14 — JS4: "Hungary’s Parliament adopted, under an accelerated procedure and without meaningful consultation, Act III of 2025, amending Act LV of 2018 on the right of assembly"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/2), para. 73 — OHCHR: "legislation passed that had resulted in arbitrary and discriminatory restrictions on the rights of LGBTIQ+ individuals to freedom of expression, peaceful assembly and privacy"

recommendations.text: Strengthen its efforts to protect and facilitate the rights to freedom of association, peaceful assembly and expression
Ensure the protection and promotion of the rights to freedom of association, peaceful assembly and expression, and ensure that the exercise of these rights does not bring prejudice
Redouble efforts to ensure full respect for the rights to freedom of association, peaceful assembly and expression, including the protection of civil society and academia

blocks.summary: Allow civil society organisations to operate freely
blocks.rationale: The National Report describes the existing framework only; stakeholders point to the Transparency of Public Life bill.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/3), para. 17 — JS5: "formally withdraw the Transparency of Public Life bill to ensure that legislation does not restrict the lawful activities of civil society"

recommendations.text: Ensure that civil society organizations can operate freely, without discrimination or undue restriction

themes.theme: Economic, social & cultural rights - general measures of implementation

blocks.summary: Visible bilingualism in the Rába region
blocks.rationale: Bilingual signage appears on public institutions throughout the Rába region and municipal offices have Slovenian-speaking staff.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/1), para. 106 — Hungary: "Bilingual signage appears on public institutions throughout the region"

recommendations.text: Fully implement visible bilingualism in the Raba region

blocks.summary: Sustainable development and youth employment
blocks.rationale: Youth Guarantee Plus and a programme for jobseekers over 30 were launched to raise employment.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/1), para. 87 — Hungary: "Policies that have been adopted to further improve the employment rate include the Youth Guarantee Plus Programme"

recommendations.text: Continue to promote sustainable economic and social development and to further promote employment

blocks.summary: Business and human rights legislation and national action plan
blocks.rationale: The documents contain no information on this recommendation.

recommendations.text: Enact legislation to conflict-affected areas and provide guidance and advice for business enterprises on ensuring respect for human rights, and prevent and address the heightened risk of corporate involvement in gross human right violations in conflict-affected areas, including situations of foreign occupation
Develop a national action plan in line with the Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights

Ensure that, in the context of the new legislation adopted in 2020, the so-called “ethno-business” phenomenon will be tackled in an efficient way and that the self-governments are true representatives of the interests of persons belonging to national minorities on whose behalf they act

blocks.summary: Reform detention with a human rights-based approach
blocks.rationale: The National Report reports no detention reform; the CPT found continued ill-treatment in Tiszalök prison and pending investigations.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/3), para. 10 — European Committee for the Prevention of Torture: "physical ill-treatment at Tiszalök prison had continued despite the Committee’s (CPT) 2023 findings"

Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/3), para. 11 — European Committee for the Prevention of Torture: "Criminal investigations into alleged prison staff misconduct, some dating back to 2020–2021, were still pending at the pre-trial stage"

recommendations.text: Make progress in the comprehensive reform of detention centres, through a human rights-based approach, and in compliance with the recommendations of the Committee against Torture

themes.theme: Prohibition of torture & ill-treatment (including cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment)

blocks.summary: Investigate excessive use of force and ill-treatment by law enforcement
blocks.rationale: The National Report is silent; the CPT reports continued allegations and slow investigations.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/3), para. 11 — European Committee for the Prevention of Torture: "Criminal investigations into alleged prison staff misconduct, some dating back to 2020–2021, were still pending at the pre-trial stage"

recommendations.text: Ensure that excessive use of force, including ill-treatment and torture by law enforcement officials at the time of arrest and during interrogations, is investigated and prosecuted, and perpetrators convicted and held accountable

blocks.summary: Strengthen the independence of the judiciary
blocks.rationale: Act X of 2023 strengthened the National Judicial Council, made the allocation of cases in the Curia transparent and removed obstacles to preliminary references to the CJEU; the Helsinki Committee calls for its effective implementation.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/1), para. 25 — Hungary: "Act X of 2023 strengthened the role and powers of the National Judicial Council (OBT) in order to balance the powers of the President of the National Judicial Office (OBH)"

Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/3), para. 12 — Hungary Helsinki Committee: "requested the effective implementation of the prerogatives of the National Judicial Council introduced by the 2023 judicial reform"

recommendations.text: Take measures to protect the full independence and impartiality of the judiciary
Implement measures to guarantee the independence of the judiciary
Safeguard and guarantee full and effective independence of the judiciary, including when it comes to the appointment of judges to the Supreme Court

Reverse the politicization of the judicial system by strengthening the National Judicial Council’s powers, instituting the random allocation of cases, and protecting judges from political pressure, criticism or retribution
Strengthen judicial independence, including by implementing the Basic Principles on the Independence of the Judiciary and strengthening the role of the National Judiciary Council
Take action to protect judicial independence by bringing the selection and appointment procedures of court presidents into line with international standards

Ensure judicial independence, including by reinforcing the National Judicial Council in line with recommendations of the Venice Commission and the Council of Europe, and fully comply with the decisions of the European Court of Human Rights and the European Court of Justice

Take measures to ensure the independence of the judiciary, including by implementing the Venice Commission’s recommendations to strengthen the national judicial council and the national judicial office and its president
Consider taking measures to strengthen the full independence, impartiality and effectiveness of the judiciary
Take effective steps to guarantee and protect full independence and impartiality of the judiciary as well as the separation of powers
Fully respect the separation of powers to ensure work will be exercised in an impartial and independent manner

themes.theme: Freedom of opinion and expression & access to information

blocks.summary: Protect media freedom and pluralism, and academic freedom
blocks.rationale: The National Report has no section on media pluralism or media regulation; the Special Rapporteur on freedom of expression still calls for a legal framework on media independence and a reformed Media Council, and the Special Rapporteur on the right to education reports an erosion of academic freedom.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/2), para. 26 — Special Rapporteur on freedom of expression: "recommended that Hungary adopt a legal and policy framework, through an inclusive multi-stakeholder process, to promote media independence and pluralism"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/2), para. 29 — Special Rapporteur on freedom of expression: "called for the independence, transparency and accountability of the Media Council, including through legislative reforms"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/3), para. 38 — Scholars at Risk: "urged Hungary to commit publicly to restoring academic freedom and related human rights"

recommendations.text: Take concrete initiatives – also at a legislative level – to ensure actual press freedom and freedom of expression
Take effective measures to ensure the promotion of media pluralism and freedom of expression
Increase efforts to ensure the freedom and independence of the media and the full right to freedom of expression
Ensure a level playing field for media by enabling editorial pluralism through independent media outlets, including the public broadcaster, and an independent media regulator
Establish more transparent appointment procedures for the Media Authority to enhance its independence
Restore media pluralism and independence and ensure freedom of expression by refraining from obstruction and intimidation of independent media outlets and journalists
Ensure independent media and media-regulating bodies, and reinforce media plurality and an enabling environment for their operation, free from undue influence, interference or intimidation

Take concrete steps to guarantee the freedom of the media and their independent work, and promote a pluralist, transparent and participatory media environment, both offline and online, including steps to ensure the independence of the media regulator
Protect civil and political rights, and repeal laws that place undue restrictions on civic space and the media
Take steps to protect freedom of expression through media pluralism, including by promoting the political independence of the media regulatory authority

blocks.summary: Protect academic freedom and university autonomy
blocks.rationale: Act XCI of 2024 on HUN-REN states the principle of scientific freedom, but the research network was institutionally altered several times and the Special Rapporteur on the right to education and Scholars at Risk report an erosion of academic freedom.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/1), para. 80 — Hungary: "the Hungarian Research Network stipulates that HUNREN pursues its scientific research and innovation activities in research institutions, in accordance with the principle of scientific freedom"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/3), para. 38 — Scholars at Risk: "urged Hungary to commit publicly to restoring academic freedom and related human rights"

recommendations.text: Ensure protection of the scientific freedom and autonomy of universities and research institutes, including autonomy in determining curricula, teaching, research and management in line with its international obligations regarding academic freedom
Take effective steps to protect freedom of expression, including of civil society actors and scholars, protect academic freedom, and ensure the autonomy of universities
Take measures to effectively protect university autonomy in line with international human rights standards relating to academic freedom

blocks.summary: Restore media independence and the independence of the Media Council
blocks.rationale: The National Report has no media section; the Special Rapporteur on freedom of expression still calls for a reformed Media Council and a framework for media independence.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/2), para. 28 — Special Rapporteur on freedom of expression: "revise the appointment procedure for the Chair of the Media Council to make it more transparent and inclusive"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/2), para. 29 — Special Rapporteur on freedom of expression: "called for the independence, transparency and accountability of the Media Council, including through legislative reforms"

recommendations.by: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
recommendations.text: Introduce legal safeguards to make the Media Council more pluralistic and free from political interference

blocks.summary: Allow civil society organisations to operate freely
blocks.rationale: The National Report describes the existing framework only; stakeholders point to the Transparency of Public Life bill.
evidence: Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/3), para. 17 — JS5: "formally withdraw the Transparency of Public Life bill to ensure that legislation does not restrict the lawful activities of civil society"

recommendations.text: Strengthen freedom of expression and association by enacting regulations that enable licensing of media outlets and ensuring civil society organizations can operate freely without interference

themes.theme: Right to participate in public affairs & right to vote

blocks.summary: Public consultation on legislation
blocks.rationale: Since 2022 the government audit body fines ministries that omit the legally required public consultation; the 8-day minimum consultation period predates the review.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/1), para. 32 — Hungary: "if the government audit body reveals that an omission has occurred in relation to the consultation process"

recommendations.text: Ensure holding consultation processes when drafting new laws, in order to allow for a timely public debate and inclusive interaction with non-State actors and free media, in accordance with target 16.7 of the Sustainable Development Goals

blocks.summary: Promote gender equality and women's representation
blocks.rationale: The National Report reports statistics on women in leadership but no measure to ensure representation.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/1), para. 36 — Hungary: "women accounted for 40% of leaders in Hungary in 2024"

recommendations.text: Continue measures to promote gender equality and ensure the representation of ethnic minorities in political and public life

themes.theme: Human trafficking & contemporary forms of slavery

blocks.summary: Combat trafficking in persons and protect victims
blocks.rationale: Hungary implemented an action plan under the 2020-2023 national strategy (prevention programmes in care institutions), earmarked HUF 1 billion under the Swiss-Hungarian programme, ran a referral mechanism exercise (July 2025) and provided for guardians for unaccompanied minors; CEDAW calls for adequate resources.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/1), para. 115 — Hungary: "introduced prevention programmes in the foster care network, children’s and group homes and juvenile correctional institutions"
National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/1), para. 116 — Hungary: "1 billion HUF is earmarked for action to combat trafficking in human beings"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/2), para. 38 — Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination against Women: "recommended that Hungary ensure sufficient human, technical and financial resources for the effective implementation and monitoring of the National Strategy against Trafficking in Human Beings for 2020–2023"

recommendations.by: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
recommendations.text: Create a specialized framework for identifying and assisting child victims of human trafficking
Continue its support in strengthening its mechanisms in protecting all persons, including children, from human trafficking
Pursue the efforts made in protecting minorities and combating human trafficking
Continue efforts to implement the national strategy to combat human trafficking for the period 2020–2023
Ensure an inclusive and multi-stakeholder approach to implementing measures to prevent and address anti-trafficking in persons

blocks.summary: Promote gender equality in the labour market and implement CEDAW
blocks.rationale: The pay gap narrowed and an implementation plan for 2025-2026 was adopted; CEDAW is deeply concerned about retrogressive movements and an equality policy based on the family role of women.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/1), para. 38 — Hungary: "Government Decision No. 393/2024 (XII.12.) promulgated the Implementation Plan for the years 2025–2026"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/2), para. 59 — Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination against Women: "was deeply concerned about retrogressive movements seeking to exclude reference to gender from the political, educational and social discourse"

recommendations.text: Continue efforts to support gender equality in the labour market and to reduce the wage gap between men and women

blocks.summary: Comply with the provisions of CEDAW
blocks.rationale: CEDAW advises adopting comprehensive anti-discrimination legislation and is concerned about retrogressive movements; no such legislation is reported.
evidence: UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/2), para. 7 — Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination against Women: "advised Hungary to adopt, with a clear time frame, comprehensive anti-discrimination legislation"

recommendations.text: Adopt measures to effectively comply with the provisions of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women

blocks.summary: Reduce poverty, especially among minorities
blocks.rationale: The National Social Inclusion Strategy 2030 and its 2025-2027 action plan target poverty eradication and Roma inclusion; JS2 calls for targeted programmes on intergenerational poverty.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/1), para. 108 — Hungary: "The two fundamental objectives of the MNTFS2030 are the eradication of poverty and the promotion of the inclusion of the Roma community"
Stakeholders' Summary (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/3), para. 55 — JS2: "recommended the development of targeted programs to reduce intergenerational poverty"

recommendations.text: Take concrete measures to end poverty
Strengthen policies to end poverty, especially for minorities

blocks.summary: Equal access to quality education, including for Roma and minority children
blocks.rationale: Hungary adopted Act XCII of 2023 on anti-discrimination measures in public education (from January 2024), supports about 700 underperforming or segregated schools, runs a dropout early-warning system and 112 minority-run institutions; the Special Rapporteur on the right to education warns of widening inequality and Roma segregation.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/1), para. 69 — Hungary: "Act XCII of 2023 on anti-discrimination measures applicable in the field of public education entered into force on 1 January 2024"
National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/1), para. 78 — Hungary: "provides methodological support to approximately 700 underperforming or segregated institutions"

UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/2), para. 44 — Special Rapporteur on the right to education: "expressing serious concern about widening inequalities, curriculum rigidity, the marginalization of Roma students and the erosion of academic freedom"

recommendations.text: Adopt more policies and allocate more resources specifically directed towards equal education for all children
Ensure that children belonging to national minorities have access to education in their mother tongue
Ensure an effective and qualitative education in minority languages at all levels of education, including by providing teachers able to teach subjects in minority languages
Pursue its efforts in promoting the right to education to ensure access to quality and inclusive education for all, including vulnerable and marginalized groups
Ensure that education is provided to all children on a non-discriminatory basis
Take further steps to strengthen access to quality early childhood education and improve educational outcomes
Address challenges in the realization of the right to education, including in the context of the high number of students leaving school early
Continue efforts to improve the quality of education and increase access to quality, inclusive and general education

blocks.summary: Combat discrimination against Roma and promote their inclusion
blocks.rationale: The National Social Inclusion Strategy 2030 (action plan 2025-2027), the Opportunity Kindergarten/School/Workshop programmes and Roma police dialogue events were launched or continued; the Special Rapporteur reports that 51% of Roma children drop out of compulsory school and that segregation is increasing.
evidence: National Report (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/1), para. 110 — Hungary: "Complex Settlement Programmes, reaching 80 segregated localities, contribute to reducing territorial inequalities and residential segregation"
UN Compilation (A/HRC/WG.6/53/HUN/2), para. 68 — Special Rapporteur on freedom of religion: "51 per cent of Roma children dropping out while still in compulsory school"

recommendations.text: Take further measures to improve access to education of Roma children
Continue measures aimed at improving education outcomes and access to quality, inclusive and mainstream education for Roma children
Guarantee equal access to education for Roma children and end their segregation in schools
Strengthen efforts to provide access to non-discriminatory and inclusive education for Roma children and take steps to improve their educational opportunities
Take measures to increase school attendance of Roma children and eradicate their discrimination in schools
Take further steps to improve education, housing and social protection of Roma, in particular children, including by addressing cases of school segregation

Prioritize initiatives to eliminate discrimination against and segregation of Roma children in schools, and take prompt measures to reduce the educational attainment gap between Roma and non-Roma children, particularly in primary education
Continue to foster the necessary measures to ensure access to education for Roma children and the elimination of segregation

paragraphs.title: Holding migrants in transit areas and immigration detention
paragraphs.recommendation: The State party should bring its legislation and practices relating to the treatment of migrants and asylum seekers into compliance with the Covenant, taking into account, inter alia, the Committee’s general comment No. 35 (2014) on liberty and security of person. It should also: (a) Refrain from automatically removing all asylum applicants to the transit areas, thereby restricting their liberty, and conduct individual assessments of the need to transfer them, on a case-by-case basis; (b) Significantly reduce the period of initial mandatory immigration detention, ensure that any detention beyond that initial period is justified as reasonable, necessary and proportionate in the light of the individual’s circumstances and provide that it is subject to periodic judicial review; (c) Expand the use of alternatives to detention for asylum seekers; (d) Legally limit the overall duration of immigration detention; (e) Provide for a meaningful right to appeal against detention and other restrictions on movement; (f) Ensure that children and unaccompanied minors are not detained, except as a measure of last resort and for the shortest appropriate period of time, taking into account their best interests, as a primary consideration, with regard to the duration and conditions of detention and their special need for care; * Adopted by the Committee at its 133rd session (11 October–5 November 2021). (g) Improve the conditions in the transit areas and ensure that migrants are held in appropriate, sanitary, non-punitive facilities and that immigration detention does not take place in prisons

limbs.eval: The Committee takes note of the information provided on the closure of transit areas within the State party. Nevertheless, it is concerned at the absence of information about the effective implementation of the legal changes described. It requests specific information on the steps that have been taken to implement the reform, including clarification of whether the provisions allowing individuals to submit a declaration of intent remain in place and how many individuals have been allowed entry into the State party’s territory each year since the introduction of those provisions. The Committee is also concerned at the lack of information about any broader efforts to limit immigration detention in law and in practice, in line with its recommendation. It requests that the State party provide further information in this regard

(f) The Committee welcomes the information provided by the State party about efforts made to ensure that children and unaccompanied minors are not detained, except as a measure of last resort and for the shortest appropriate period of time, taking into account their best interests. It requests further information about the specific steps taken within the reporting period to step up safeguards against detaining children and unaccompanied minors

paragraphs.title: Non-refoulement and excessive use of force
paragraphs.recommendation: The State party should ensure that the non-refoulement principle is secured in law and strictly adhered to in practice, and that all asylum seekers, regardless of their mode of arrival into Hungary, have access to fair and efficient refugee status determination procedures and effective protection against non-refoulement. In particular, it should: (a) Repeal the pushback law adopted in June 2016 and the amendments thereto, and legally ensure that the removal of an individual must always be consistent with the State party’s non-refoulement obligations; (b) Consider revising Decree No. 191/2015 and developing procedural safeguards against refoulement, including the possibility of the review of asylum decisions by an independent judicial body that can provide effective remedies; (c) Refrain from the collective expulsion of aliens and conduct an objective, individualized assessment of the level of protection available in “safe third countries”; (d) Ensure that force or physical restraint is not applied against migrants, except under strict conditions of necessity and proportionality, that all allegations of the use of force against them are promptly investigated, that perpetrators are prosecuted and punished with appropriate sanctions and that victims are offered reparation

limbs.eval: The Committee takes note of the information provided by the State party on the instruments within the national legal framework, including the Fundamental Law of Hungary, providing for protection for refugees and asylum seekers from countries that do not meet the criteria to be deemed safe. Nevertheless, it regrets the lack of information on the status of the pushback law adopted in June 2016 and any steps taken by the State party to repeal this legislation. The Committee reiterates its recommendation and requests information on the status of this legislation. While taking note of the information provided by the State party on the procedures in place to prevent refoulement, the Committee is concerned at the lack of information about any concrete measures that have been taken during the reporting period to revise Decree No. 191/2015 and to develop procedural safeguards against refoulement. The Committee takes note of the information provided by the State party indicating that thirdcountry nationals can be expelled only when their application for asylum is refused by a final and executable decision of the Directorate-General for Aliens Policing. Nevertheless, it regrets the absence of information on any specific measures taken to end the practice of collective expulsions of aliens. The Committee takes note of the information provided by the State party on the legal provisions in place to regulate the use of force by law enforcement officials. It welcomes the fact that allegations of ill-treatment have been forwarded to the prosecutor’s office. However, it remains concerned about the lack of information regarding investigations into these allegations and about the prosecutions secured for ill-treatment of migrants, the sanctions applied to the perpetrators and the remedies provided to the victims. It reiterates its recommendation in this regard and requests information on the number of complaints received during the reporting period and their outcomes

paragraphs.title: “Stop-Soros” package
paragraphs.recommendation: The State party should reject the draft laws known as the “Stop-Soros” package introduced before the parliament on 13 February 2018 and ensure that all legislation relating to NGOs is fully consistent with its international obligations under the Covenant, reflects the important role of NGOs in a democratic society and is designed to facilitate, not undermine, their operations

limbs.eval: The Committee takes note of the information provided by the State party on the withdrawal of the draft laws and cooperation with civil society organizations. Nevertheless, it regrets the lack of detail about when and under what circumstances draft laws T/19776, T/19775 and T/19774 were withdrawn. The Committee requests specific information on when the laws were withdrawn and on the overall legislative framework relating to nongovernmental organizations, particularly those working in support of the rights of refugees, asylum seekers and migrants, including any reform enacted during the reporting period
